name: update_record_output_block
description: Copies a record's pending state into a hardware-style output block and scales a value by a table entry, then clears the pending flag and updates the record's counters. It also touches the DMA and interrupt control registers and calls a one-instruction routine that merges a constant into a register.

name: run_countdown_trigger_sequence
description: Calls three routines in order, then, when a flag word is set, decrements a byte countdown and calls a further routine when the countdown reaches zero. It returns the last value produced.

name: tick_record_countdown
description: Checks a record's enable word and, when it is set, decrements a byte countdown stored in the record. It calls a routine when the countdown expires and a target pointer is present, and otherwise returns the incoming register value.

name: step_level_ramp_stages
description: Advances a three-stage level ramp: the first stage steps the level up by a table step until a limit is reached, the second steps it down, and then the level holds at a table value. Stage parameters are read through the record pointer.

name: initialize_audio_channels
description: Clears the control registers of all four audio channels, then sets their period, volume and data pointer values and copies a block of words into a table for later channel setup. It also writes the DMA, interrupt and audio control registers.

name: repeat_call_until_zero
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until it returns zero, then returns with the register values unchanged.

name: initialize_record_slot_from_table
description: Initialises one channel record selected by index: it clears the record's workspace, copies setup words and pointers into it and marks the slot as active. It also touches the background colour, DMA and interrupt registers, and loops forever when the table entry is empty.

name: load_record_parameters
description: Stores parameter words from a source table into a record and writes an initial set of words and a pointer into a destination block. It sets the record's period and volume defaults.

name: manage_dma_and_interrupts
description: A 128-instruction routine that writes the DMA control and the interrupt enable and request registers and calls four other routines; thirteen routines call it. The decompiler timed out, so its detailed logic is not recovered.

name: call_one_routine_stub
description: A three-instruction stub that makes a single call to another routine and returns. No further logic is recovered from it.

name: call_one_routine_short
description: A two-instruction stub that makes a single call to another routine. No further logic is recovered from it.

name: call_one_routine_brief
description: A five-instruction routine that makes a single call to another routine. The decompiler timed out, so no further logic is recovered.

name: call_one_routine_relay
description: A five-instruction routine that relays a single call to another routine. The decompiler timed out, so no further logic is recovered.

name: call_one_routine_block
description: A twelve-instruction routine that makes a single call to another routine. It is not reached by the reference run, and no further logic is recovered.

name: call_one_routine_sequence
description: A twenty-instruction routine that makes a single call to another routine. The decompiler timed out, so no further logic is recovered.

name: call_one_routine_tiny
description: A two-instruction stub that makes a single call to another routine. It is not reached by the reference run, and no further logic is recovered.

name: call_one_routine_quick
description: A four-instruction stub that makes a single call to another routine. No further logic is recovered from it.

name: call_two_routines_stub
description: A five-instruction routine that makes two calls to other routines. It is not reached by the reference run, and no further logic is recovered.

name: call_one_routine_leaf
description: A three-instruction routine that makes a single call to another routine and is called from one other routine. No further logic is recovered.

name: call_one_routine_checked
description: A ten-instruction routine that makes a single call to another routine. The decompiler timed out, so no further logic is recovered.

name: call_one_routine_compact
description: A six-instruction routine that makes a single call to another routine and is called from one other routine. No further logic is recovered.

name: copy_word_pair_three_times
description: Copies two word fields from one part of a record to another part, repeating the pair three times and stepping through the record by two bytes each time.

name: copy_word_pair_twice
description: Copies two word fields from one part of a record to another part, repeating the pair twice and stepping through the record by two bytes each time.

name: run_screen_setup_and_jump
description: Initialises a set of globals, calls several routines to prepare the screen named in the referenced text, and ends with an indirect jump through a computed address. A flag test chooses between two setup paths.

name: stub_infinite_loop_wait
description: A stub that never returns: the decompiler shows only an infinite loop. The facts show it touches the background colour and DMA control registers, but no other behaviour is recovered.

name: store_word_delta_and_update
description: Computes the difference between two stored words, saves it into a second word, and then copies the newer word into the older slot.

name: return_only_stub
description: A single return instruction that does nothing; one routine calls it.

name: copy_block_then_halt
description: Sets a flag, copies a block of longwords from one fixed address to another, calls nine routines in sequence, and then loops forever without returning. The decompiler removed many unreachable blocks.

name: call_routine_at_offsets
description: Calls a routine repeatedly, passing pairs of values offset from its incoming values, and returns the final pair. The routine is not reached by the reference run, and the callee's role is not recovered.

name: call_routines_with_table_value
description: Looks up a 16-bit value in a table selected by bits of a global variable, then calls a routine three times with offsets derived from the incoming values and that table value.

name: reset_state_and_copy_block
description: Clears a set of state words and sets others according to two flag values, then copies a block of words from one area of memory to another.

name: blit_shifted_row_segments
description: Sets up blitter operations for a row of an image: it computes source and destination addresses, builds shift masks from a table, waits for the blitter to be free before each start, and writes the control and modulo registers. It uses a routine routine to prepare its structure.

name: prepare_blit_row_record
description: Writes blitter control words, masks and addresses into a record and starts blitter operations for a shifted row, waiting for the blitter to be free first. It is a shorter variant of a sibling routine that uses the same tables.

name: set_mode_parameters_by_flag
description: Sets four words from constants, with one of the words chosen by whether a global variable is nonzero.

name: return_only_stub_alt
description: A single return instruction that does nothing; it is called from one routine.

name: empty_stub_routine
description: A routine with no operations that returns immediately and is called from one routine.

name: load_hunk_sections_with_relocations
description: Reads AmigaDOS load-file records, allocates memory for each code and data section, copies the section contents, applies 32-bit relocation entries, and stops at the end marker. Memory allocation and free calls from the operating system library are used.

name: bit_test_return_stub
description: Tests whether the upper bits of a shift register are nonzero and returns in either case. The body does nothing, so it is effectively a stub.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (1992)(mindscape)[cr skr](disk 1 of 3)(install)[a]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (1992)(Mindscape)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 3)(Install)[a].adf:shut.exe:0:0082
name: shift_bits_out_of_register
description: Shifts a bit register one bit at a time for a counted number of steps, refilling it from memory with the carried-in bit when it empties.

name: setup_copper_display_program
description: Opens and closes operating-system libraries, clears a block of memory, copies table data into a copper list, points the copper at that list and waits in a loop on an interrupt flag. It also reads the CIA port and writes the DMA and interrupt control registers.

name: copy_nested_word_table_block
description: Copies a rectangular table of words row by row into a destination buffer, using nested counted loops over a fixed table offset.

name: fill_strided_table_entries
description: Fills entries spaced a fixed stride apart with a byte taken from a lookup table, advancing through the table for a fixed number of iterations and updating a stored offset.

name: blit_rows_from_index_table
description: Waits for the blitter to be free, sets its mask, modulo and size words, then runs a fixed number of blit operations whose source offsets come from a lookup table, advancing a stored index each time.

name: advance_frame_table_and_blit
description: Counts down a frame timer; when it expires, reads the next code from a sequence, finds its column in a table of fixed-width rows, and copies the values to two destinations. It then programs the blitter twice.

name: advance_counter_and_check_limit
description: Waits for the blitter, starts a blitter operation, calls two routines and increments a counter. When the counter reaches a set limit it advances a second counter and returns a failure code once that exceeds a threshold, otherwise it returns zero.

name: start_blit_with_masks_a
description: Waits for the blitter to be free, sets its first and last word masks and control word, stores two address pointers, and starts a blit of a fixed size.

name: start_blit_with_swapped_pointers
description: Waits for the blitter to be free, sets its mask and control words, stores the two address pointers in swapped order, and starts a blit of a fixed size.

name: refresh_slot_table_from_sequence
description: Maintains eight slot records. On the first call it initialises the slot table and clears a block of memory; on later calls it refills slots from a byte sequence and copies table columns into a destination buffer, calling three routines for each slot. It also reads the CIA register block.

name: encode_four_byte_entry
description: Writes a four-byte entry derived from two input values: one byte from a value offset by a constant, a flag in the fourth byte, and two bytes computed from the other input. The output goes to the record the caller points to.

name: copy_record_bytes_to_buffer
description: Copies seven bytes from a record into a buffer at a position computed from two inputs, placing them at a fixed row stride.

name: clear_state_block_and_call
description: Clears a block of state bytes starting at a global address, then calls one routine.

name: build_pointer_table_from_offsets
description: Adds a fixed base address to seven stored values and stores them in slots. It then fills a pointer table with cumulative addresses computed from a list of relative offsets.

name: reset_audio_state_from_entry
description: Disables interrupts and DMA through their control registers, clears the four audio volume registers, copies a twelve-byte entry from a table into the state block, clears the state block, and sets three state words.

name: clear_state_return_input
description: Clears a block of state bytes, sets one state byte to a fixed value and clears an audio volume register, then returns the incoming value unchanged.

name: call_routine_between_flag_set
description: Clears a flag word, calls one routine, then sets the flag word to all ones.

name: set_pending_state_words
description: Copies one stored word into another, stores the incoming register value into a second word, and sets a flag word to one. The routine is not reached by the reference run.

name: reset_flag_and_clear_state
description: Clears a flag word and the state block, then calls one routine.

name: step_audio_sequence_counter
description: Advances a counter and, when it reaches its limit, resets it and calls a routine if a flag is set. Four channel flag bytes are checked, and the audio pointer and DMA control registers are written by the routines it calls.

name: compute_table_pointer_entry
description: Reads a selector from a record. When the selector is one it stores the address of a routine; otherwise it stores a pointer computed from a global table entry and a scaled index, together with the selector value.

name: dispatch_flagged_update_routines
description: Calls two routines unconditionally, then calls further routines for each nonzero flag among three words, and returns the result of a final conditional call. It also sets a global word to a fixed high-bit value.

name: advance_index_load_entry
description: Increments a counter and, when it reaches its limit, resets it, advances an index with wraparound, and copies four longwords from the table entry at that index into four global variables.

name: load_flagged_table_values
description: For each of four flags that is nonzero, loads a longword from a lookup table at an index stored in a global and writes it to a matching global variable.

name: decode_command_word_switch
description: Decodes a 16-bit command word through a switch on its high bits: most cases store a value into a state field and return it, some return a sentinel, and one case updates timing and volume fields. The decompiler output is cut short, so the full set of cases is not recovered.

name: call_unresolved_jump_table
description: Makes an indirect call through an address the decompiler could not recover from a jump table, then returns.

name: return_only_stub
description: A single return instruction that does nothing and is reached only through its address being taken.

name: store_word_into_record
description: Stores the incoming word into a fixed field of a record and returns. The code is a gap decoded as a routine, and the reference run does not reach it.

name: apply_command_position_update
description: Decodes the high byte of a packed command word: some values call routines, while others update a pair of stored position words and a record index, clearing a 61-byte block in one case. It calls six routines and touches the DMA control register according to the facts.

name: store_table_entry_or_clear
description: Looks up a longword in a table selected by a stored index. When it is zero, it calls a routine and clears a byte; otherwise it stores the value and a word offset derived from a stored field, then sets the byte to all ones.

name: copy_strided_record_rows
description: Copies rows of a record block from a table into a destination buffer four longwords at a time, storing the destination address and a length word, and clears a byte when it finishes.

name: load_entry_fields_into_record
description: Selects a table entry by a stored index and copies several word fields from it into a record, resetting the record's counters to zero.

name: copy_entry_fields_into_record
description: Copies a group of word fields from a table entry passed in directly into a record and clears its counters.

name: clear_record_output_fields
description: Clears an output word, two record fields and a stored index, then clears a flag byte.

name: run_four_update_routines
description: Calls four routines in sequence and returns. The facts show that the audio pointer registers for channels zero to three are written through those routines.

name: update_record_output_level
description: Advances a record's sequence position and moves its level toward a target value using a division by a stored step count. It writes an output word and a level byte, and returns early when its enable word is zero. The routine is long, so only its main steps are described.

name: run_mode_processing_on_countdown
description: Counts down a record's timer and, when it expires, reloads it and performs one of several byte operations chosen by a mode word, such as negating a byte, adding a constant to a range or copying bytes. The decompiler output is cut short, so only the first cases are recovered.

name: call_unresolved_jump_table
description: Makes an indirect call through an address the decompiler could not recover from a jump table, then returns.

name: negate_byte_and_advance_index
description: Negates the byte at a record's current index, advances that index, and wraps it back to a start value when it passes the end.

name: return_failure_code
description: A program entry that immediately returns minus one to its caller.

name: call_library_entry
description: Calls one routine and checks the zero flag. If the flag is not set, it calls a second routine, calls a function pointer taken from a global table, and then calls a third routine before returning. The library call at a fixed offset is also used.

name: open_dos_library
description: Opens the DOS library through the operating system's old-style open call and stores the library handle in a global variable. The referenced text is the library name.

name: setup_dos_command_context
description: Clears a block of workspace longwords, opens the operating-system and DOS libraries through function-pointer calls, and then either sets up a context from a configured entry or builds a quoted command string in newly allocated memory. Directory, lock, file, memory and message calls from the operating-system library are used.

name: release_dos_resources
description: Calls a stored cleanup routine if one is set, then either tears down a library handle set through close and unlock calls or releases memory and reply messages. It uses DOS and exec library calls to close files, unlock locks and free memory.

name: free_linked_node_list
description: Walks a linked list of nodes, calling a release routine for each node, then clears the list head and the node count.

name: split_command_line_arguments
description: Splits a command string into up to thirty-two argument pointers, honouring double-quoted arguments and star-prefixed escape codes that become control characters. It then initialises state words from the parsed count and a set of library handles.

name: call_function_pointer
description: Loads a function pointer from a fixed offset in a global data structure and calls the code it points to.

name: return_only_stub
description: A single return instruction that does nothing; it is called from one routine.

name: empty_stub_routine
description: A routine with no operations that returns immediately and is called from one routine.

name: resolve_handle_with_status
description: Calls a routine to obtain a handle, returning minus one when the handle is zero. Otherwise it calls a routine when a flag bit in the handle is set, obtains a value from another routine, and returns minus one if a stored field is nonzero.

name: emit_string_to_bounded_buffer
description: Writes a string into a buffer while a remaining-length counter allows, calling a routine for characters past the limit, and returns the number of characters in the string. The referenced text includes a hexadecimal digit table, the null device name and a console window specification, and the input and output streams are opened through DOS calls.

name: prompt_and_dispatch_user_choice
description: Reads characters until one of two command letters is pressed, then runs one of two paths: one reads and matches a path string and may run a sub-command, the other runs a list of steps through library call pointers. The facts report only one instruction, which conflicts with the decompiled body, so this description is less certain.

name: allocate_record_if_unset
description: When a record's pointer is empty or a flag bit is set, calls a routine to allocate a buffer and stores the result in two fields. A failed allocation sets an error code and returns minus one; otherwise the routine returns zero.

name: write_character_with_line_state
description: Writes a character into an output buffer while tracking line state: a newline is written as a carriage return followed by the newline, and a column count and status flags are updated. It calls routines when the buffer is full or padding is needed, and is called from three routines.

name: read_next_buffered_character
description: Returns the next byte from a buffer, treating a carriage-return pair and an end-of-file marker specially. When the buffer is empty it fetches more input through a routine, records status flags, and returns minus one at the end of input.

name: read_buffered_character_refill
description: Reads the next buffered character with the same logic as its sibling routine. It calls four routines.

name: flush_pending_entries
description: Walks a table of entries from the last to the first and calls a routine for each entry that is enabled and lacks a particular flag bit, then calls one more routine.

name: copy_three_bytes_into_record
description: Copies three bytes from a source into a record and then locates a second three-byte group with a routine, storing it with a presence flag. The referenced text is a short name string.

name: append_bounded_string
description: Appends a source string to the end of a destination string, copying at most the number of characters given in a register, and terminates the result.

name: copy_string_returning_end
description: Copies a null-terminated string into a destination buffer, including the terminator, and returns a pointer to the terminating position.

name: format_signed_integer
description: Writes the decimal form of a signed value into a buffer: a minus sign is written first when the value is negative, digits come from a routine and are reversed into place, and a null terminator is added. It returns the number of characters written.

name: parse_signed_decimal_prefix
description: Parses an optional sign and decimal digits from the start of a string into a stored integer and returns the number of characters consumed. The routine is larger and its listing references directory examine, lock and error calls, but the decompiled body shown only covers the number parsing.

name: return_block_to_free_list
description: Returns a block of memory to a sorted free list, rounding the size up to a multiple of four bytes with a minimum of eight. It merges the block with adjacent free blocks and returns zero, or minus one when the size is invalid or the block overlaps a free block.

name: call_with_error_check
description: Calls a routine and returns minus one when it returns zero. Otherwise it calls a second routine and returns minus one if an error code field is nonzero.

name: call_with_parameter_error_check
description: Calls a routine and returns minus one when it returns zero. Otherwise it calls a second routine with the incoming parameter and returns minus one if an error code field is nonzero.

name: allocate_and_link_node
description: Allocates a node through a memory routine and, when that succeeds, stores a size word and links the node into a list, updating its head and tail pointers. It returns null when the allocation fails.

name: allocate_block_from_free_list
description: Searches a free list for a block of at least the requested size, rounded to a multiple of four bytes with a minimum of eight. An exact fit is removed from the list and a larger block is split with the remainder kept on the list. When no block fits, it requests more memory through routines and returns null if that fails.

name: flush_open_handle_list
description: Walks a list of open entries, calling a routine for each entry that has a particular flag state and a changed value, then calls one further routine.

name: write_with_error_code
description: Clears the error code, calls a stored hook first if one is set, then writes through a DOS function. On failure it records the operating-system error code and sets a general error code of five, and returns the write result.

name: seek_within_file
description: Clears the error code and seeks in an open file, recording the operating-system error code when the seek fails. When the mode argument equals two, it performs a second seek call.

name: read_from_file_with_error
description: Clears the error code, reads from an open file through a DOS call, and on failure records the operating-system error code and sets a general error code of five.

name: open_file_with_error
description: Clears the error code, opens a file through a DOS call, and on failure records the operating-system error code with a general error code of two and returns minus one. Other library calls appear in the listing but are not in the decompiled body.

name: probe_lock_then_open
description: Attempts to lock a name; when the lock succeeds it releases it and returns minus one. Otherwise it tries to open the name and records an error when that also fails.

name: delete_locked_file_then_open
description: Attempts to lock a name; when the lock succeeds it releases the lock and deletes the file. It then tries to open the name, recording an error and returning minus one when the open fails.

name: close_file_handle
description: Calls a stored hook when one is set, closes the file through a DOS call, and returns zero.

name: compute_fixed_point_product
description: Multiplies two 32-bit fixed-point values held in registers, combining the high-half and low-half 16-bit products into a 32-bit result.

name: divide_with_sign_dispatch
description: Divides one signed 32-bit value by another by handling the signs of both inputs and delegating the magnitude work to routines. A negative dividend makes the result negative.

name: normalize_fixed_point_divide
description: Divides a 32-bit dividend by a 32-bit divisor using a normalised fixed-point method. It returns a 64-bit result with the quotient in the high 32 bits and the remainder in the low 32 bits.

name: copy_bounded_line_and_prompt
description: Copies up to seventy-nine characters from a stored string into a local buffer and terminates it. It then looks up a record: if the record has a pending value it writes the buffer and a newline through DOS and returns minus one, otherwise it calls a routine with the buffer.

name: copy_line_and_check_break
description: Copies a null-terminated string into a local buffer and terminates it. If a record has a pending value it writes the buffer and a newline through DOS and returns minus one; otherwise it calls a routine with the buffer. The referenced text is a break notice shown in the console.

name: acquire_handle_and_setup
description: Calls a routine to obtain a value, stores it in a local field and passes it with fixed arguments to a routine. It returns zero when the routine reports success and minus one otherwise. The referenced text is the intuition library name.

name: setup_with_local_buffer
description: Passes a local buffer and fixed arguments to a routine and returns zero when the routine reports success, otherwise minus one.

name: return_zero_unreliable_body
description: The decompiled body is only a return of zero, although the listing has seventy-seven instructions and several library calls, so this routine's behaviour is not reliably recovered. It is called from five routines.

name: lookup_slot_entry_by_index
description: Returns the address of a slot entry for a valid index whose entry is in use. Otherwise it records an error code and returns zero.

name: check_drive_status_callback
description: Reads a status word through a library call and, when a particular status bit pair is set and a callback is registered, runs the callback. When the callback reports success it clears the callback and calls one routine. The referenced text contains prompts about installing to a hard drive or floppies, labelling disks and creating a file, and the listing also uses directory and device calls.

name: process_expired_pending_entries
description: Walks a table of pending entries and, for each entry not yet marked, compares a timer with a threshold of twenty thousand units. When the timer has expired it records the time, allocates a buffer and marks the entry. It returns one when any entry was processed and minus one otherwise.

name: process_entry_list_paths
description: Loops over a list of entries and, for each unmarked entry, builds a path from stored name fields and calls routines that format and record it before marking the entry done. It frees memory through the operating-system library and references the text diskinfo. The decompiled output is long, so only the main loop is described.

name: send_request_and_wait_reply
description: Allocates a message structure, fills its fields, sends it through the operating-system message calls and waits for the reply. It returns the reply value stored in the message and frees the message afterwards.

name: flush_open_handle_list
description: Walks a list of open entries, calling a routine for each entry that has a particular flag state and a changed value, then calls one further routine.

name: release_slot_entry_if_ready
description: Looks up an entry and returns minus one when it is absent. If a flag bit is clear it calls a routine, clears a word, and returns zero unless an error code is set; otherwise it clears the word and returns zero.

name: emit_string_to_bounded_buffer
description: Writes a string into a buffer while a remaining-length counter allows, calling a routine for characters past the limit, and returns the number of characters in the string.

name: stub_undecoded_single_instruction
description: A single-instruction routine called from one place. The decompiler timed out, so no further behaviour is recovered from the listing.

name: build_device_path_name
description: Builds a path in a buffer: it appends a colon when a device flag is set and the colon is missing, appends a separator when the name does not already end in one, and appends a period followed by the result of a routine when a suffix flag is set.

name: clear_slot_entry
description: Releases a slot entry: when its pointer is set it calls a routine, then marks the entry's flag byte and value word as cleared and calls two further routines.

name: call_with_error_check
description: Calls a routine and returns minus one when it returns zero. Otherwise it calls a second routine and returns minus one if an error code field is nonzero.

name: call_handle_with_mode_flag
description: Obtains a handle through a routine and returns minus one when it is zero. Otherwise it calls a routine with the argument two when a flag bit is set, calls a further routine, and returns minus one if an error code is nonzero.

name: fill_info_block_from_flags
description: Fills a file information block from a set of option bits and stored fields, calling routines to obtain values. When a call fails it maps several operating-system error codes to general error codes and returns minus one.

name: allocate_slot_and_store_result
description: Searches a slot table from its fourth entry for a free slot and records an error if none is free. It then processes the requested mode bits through routines and stores the resulting pair in the slot; an invalid mode sets an error code and returns minus one.

name: format_string_with_arguments
description: Interprets a format string with conversions for decimal numbers, pointer-like values, strings and fixed-width digit output, writing the characters through a routine. It returns the number of characters written.

name: append_string_unbounded
description: Appends a null-terminated source string to the end of a destination string, including the terminator.

name: create_queue_node
description: Requests a value from a routine and, when it is valid, allocates a node, stores the given pointer and a flag byte, and links it into a list. A null parent creates a new list head, otherwise the node is queued on the parent. It returns zero when no value or memory is available.

name: multiply_fixed_point_values
description: Multiplies two 32-bit fixed-point values held in registers, combining the high-half and low-half 16-bit products into a 32-bit result.

name: read_line_into_buffer
description: Reads bytes from an input stream into a buffer until a newline or end-of-input marker is reached, then terminates the buffer. The newline itself is not stored.

name: undecoded_routine_ten_instructions
description: A ten-instruction routine referenced by address and called from two places. The decompiler timed out, so no behaviour is recovered from the listing.

description: Reads AmigaDOS load-file records, allocates memory for each code and data section, copies the section contents, applies 32-bit relocation entries, and stops at the end marker. Memory allocation and free calls from the operating system library are used.

description: Counts a 16-bit register down to zero in a tight loop and returns, so it waits a fixed number of iterations. It is called from two routines and calls one routine.

description: Stores the address of one global into four pointer slots and calls two routines, touching the custom chip register block as well. It returns after those calls.

name: bit_test_return_stub
description: Tests whether the upper bits of a shift register are nonzero and returns in either case. The body does nothing, so it is effectively a stub.

name: shift_bits_out_of_register
description: Shifts a bit register one bit at a time for a counted number of steps, refilling it from memory with the carried-in bit when it empties.

name: setup_copper_display_program
description: Opens and closes operating-system libraries, clears a block of memory, copies table data into a copper list, points the copper at that list and waits in a loop on an interrupt flag. It also reads the CIA port and writes the DMA and interrupt control registers.

name: copy_nested_word_table_block
description: Copies a rectangular table of words row by row into a destination buffer, using nested counted loops over a fixed table offset.

name: fill_strided_table_entries
description: Fills entries spaced a fixed stride apart with a byte taken from a lookup table, advancing through the table for a fixed number of iterations and updating a stored offset.

name: blit_rows_from_index_table
description: Waits for the blitter to be free, sets its mask, modulo and size words, then runs a fixed number of blit operations whose source offsets come from a lookup table, advancing a stored index each time.

name: advance_frame_table_and_blit
description: Counts down a frame timer; when it expires, reads the next code from a sequence, finds its column in a table of fixed-width rows, and copies the values to two destinations. It then programs the blitter twice.

name: advance_counter_and_check_limit
description: Waits for the blitter, starts a blitter operation, calls two routines and increments a counter. When the counter reaches a set limit it advances a second counter and returns a failure code once that exceeds a threshold, otherwise it returns zero.

name: start_blit_with_masks_a
description: Waits for the blitter to be free, sets its first and last word masks and control word, stores two address pointers, and starts a blit of a fixed size.

name: start_blit_with_swapped_pointers
description: Waits for the blitter to be free, sets its mask and control words, stores the two address pointers in swapped order, and starts a blit of a fixed size.

name: refresh_slot_table_from_sequence
description: Maintains eight slot records. On the first call it initialises the slot table and clears a block of memory; on later calls it refills slots from a byte sequence and copies table columns into a destination buffer, calling three routines for each slot. It also reads the CIA register block.

name: encode_four_byte_entry
description: Writes a four-byte entry derived from two input values: one byte from a value offset by a constant, a flag in the fourth byte, and two bytes computed from the other input. The output goes to the record the caller points to.

name: copy_record_bytes_to_buffer
description: Copies seven bytes from a record into a buffer at a position computed from two inputs, placing them at a fixed row stride.

name: clear_state_block_and_call
description: Clears a block of state bytes starting at a global address, then calls one routine.

name: build_pointer_table_from_offsets
description: Adds a fixed base address to seven stored values and stores them in slots. It then fills a pointer table with cumulative addresses computed from a list of relative offsets.

name: reset_audio_state_from_entry
description: Disables interrupts and DMA through their control registers, clears the four audio volume registers, copies a twelve-byte entry from a table into the state block, clears the state block, and sets three state words.

name: clear_state_return_input
description: Clears a block of state bytes, sets one state byte to a fixed value and clears an audio volume register, then returns the incoming value unchanged.

name: call_routine_between_flag_set
description: Clears a flag word, calls one routine, then sets the flag word to all ones.

name: set_pending_state_words
description: Copies one stored word into another, stores the incoming register value into a second word, and sets a flag word to one. The routine is not reached by the reference run.

name: reset_flag_and_clear_state
description: Clears a flag word and the state block, then calls one routine.

name: step_audio_sequence_counter
description: Advances a counter and, when it reaches its limit, resets it and calls a routine if a flag is set. Four channel flag bytes are checked, and the audio pointer and DMA control registers are written by the routines it calls.

name: compute_table_pointer_entry
description: Reads a selector from a record. When the selector is one it stores the address of a routine; otherwise it stores a pointer computed from a global table entry and a scaled index, together with the selector value.

name: dispatch_flagged_update_routines
description: Calls two routines unconditionally, then calls further routines for each nonzero flag among three words, and returns the result of a final conditional call. It also sets a global word to a fixed high-bit value.

name: advance_index_load_entry
description: Increments a counter and, when it reaches its limit, resets it, advances an index with wraparound, and copies four longwords from the table entry at that index into four global variables.

name: load_flagged_table_values
description: For each of four flags that is nonzero, loads a longword from a lookup table at an index stored in a global and writes it to a matching global variable.

name: decode_command_word_switch
description: Decodes a 16-bit command word through a switch on its high bits: most cases store a value into a state field and return it, some return a sentinel, and one case updates timing and volume fields. The decompiler output is cut short, so the full set of cases is not recovered.

name: call_unresolved_jump_table
description: Makes an indirect call through an address the decompiler could not recover from a jump table, then returns.
